# FreetoShop — Clone Stamp Foundation (Milestone 1)

## Task
Implement a Photoshop-familiar Clone Stamp tool in the retouch/painting toolbar family for FreetoShop, a local-first browser image editor with a tiled architecture. This is the first milestone of a multi-milestone engineering goal.

## Current state
- Inspecting the repository architecture. Found a monorepo with `apps/web` (browser app) and many packages: `core-document`, `command-history`, `compositor`, `renderer`, `raster-engine`, `selection-engine`, `filter-engine`, `transform-engine`, `text-engine`, `file-codecs`, `persistence`, `pixel-storage`, `benchmarks`.
- Key architectural files read: `ARCHITECTURE.md` (partial), `DOCUMENT_MODEL.md` (partial), `apps/web/src/tools/toolRegistry.ts` (read).
- Architecture summary: FreetoShop is browser-only, local-first, under phased development. `core-document` owns serializable editor state, layer ordering, stable IDs, invertible affine layer transforms, validated edits, editable shape geometry/styles, text content/styles, ordered typed layer effects, smart-object source trees, smart-filter state, nondestructive canvas geometry. Crop/Canvas Size change canvas bounds; translate only root-layer world placement; remap canvas-sized selection/channel data without trimming layer-local pixels/masks. Pixel layers own immutable sparse `TiledPixelStore` resources; patches replace only changed tiles; history may share unchanged resources. Raster masks use one-channel `TiledCoverageStore` with copy-on-write mask patches.
- `command-history` applies undoable commands and owns undo/redo history.
- `compositor` owns DOM-free premultiplied-alpha source-over equations, 20 separable and 6 RGB-vector professional blend modes, immutable/in-place same-sized surface composition.
- `renderer` turns document+viewport into Canvas 2D pixels; must not mutate document; rasterizes affine pixel/rectangle/ellipse/path/structured text layers; resolves clipping and group isolation; rasterizes local and document-space raster/vector masks (including masks over combined pass-through and isolated group results); recursively composites smart...

## Milestone 1 requirements (Clone Stamp foundation)
- Alt/Option-click establishes a clone source; UI clearly indicates whether a source exists.
- Pointer painting samples pixels from source and writes into destination using existing brush/raster workflow.
- Aligned mode preserves source-to-destination offset throughout a gesture and across stroke segments.
- Unaligned mode restarts sampling from source origin as required by tool convention.
- Clone sampling and destination writes use correct transformed-layer coordinate mapping.
- Operation respects active selection and clips writes to selected region.
- Operation respects current mask/edit-target model; does not write to wrong layer or mask.
- A single pointer gesture creates one atomic undoable history transaction. Undo/redo restore exact pixels and layer state.
- Saving/reopening or existing local recovery path preserves edited pixels and relevant document state.
- Missing source state handled visibly and safely; painting without a source must not silently corrupt pixels.
- Clone source, aligned/unaligned behavior, and coordinate relationship must be represented by an explicit testable data model (not implicit UI-handler state).
- Reuse tiled stores and coordinate helpers. Do not materialize entire canvas or layer for a clone operation.
- Add focused unit tests for: source/destination pixel correctness, multi-segment aligned strokes, unaligned restart, transformed layers, selection clipping, masks/edit targets, tile-boundary behavior.
- Add a browser workflow using real pointer/keyboard events; verify undo/redo plus persistence or recovery.
- Do not regress existing Brush or Eraser behavior.

## Constraints (from product/architecture)
- Editing operations are real, undoable transactions; compatible with existing command/history model.
- Pixel storage, selections, masks, channels, compositing, persistence remain tile- or region-oriented. Reads/writes/allocation/rendering bounded by affected region when operation permits.
- Preserve copy-on-write behavior and immutable historical state. Operation must not mutate unrelated layer, source document, cached tile, or prior history entry.
- Preserve existing Brush and Eraser workflows while adding neighboring tools.
- Preserve local-first behavior, browser compatibility, recovery behavior, existing file/document model.
- Use existing coordinate, raster, worker, renderer, persistence, and UI infrastructure where it is the correct extension point. Avoid broad rewrites merely to make a feature easier.
- Every visible control, menu item, shortcut, panel, or tool option must be connected to observable behavior and covered by a test at the most appropriate level.
- Keep CPU/software behavior as correctness oracle when adding optional accelerated paths. Unsupported hardware must retain valid software path.
- Document limitations honestly.

## Raster-engine internals now visible (from full index.ts read)
- `paintStroke(layer, points, options, selection?, worldTransform?)` returns `PixelPatch`. Validates layer/transform/selection/options; interpolates dabs along segments by spacing `max(0.25, radius*0.5)`; computes stroke working set as union of `localDabBounds` only (no full-layer densify); reads one region from `layer.pixelStore.read(...)`; for each dab iterates local bounds, maps each local pixel to document point via `transformPoint(worldTransform, x, y)`, computes falloff from dab distance, multiplies by opacity/pressure/selection coverage, then either erases alpha or composites source-over; tracks `changedBounds`; returns `makePatchFromRegion(...)`.
- `paintMaskStroke(mask, layerTransform, points, options, selection?)` returns `CoveragePatch`. Same dab interpolation and bounded working-set pattern; operates on mask `coverageStore.read(...)`; strength = falloff*opacity*pressure*selected; target 255 for reveal, 0 for conceal; returns coverage patch.
- `compositeSourceOver(pixels, offset, color, coverage)` does standard source-over with premultiplied-style blending; `dabCoverage(distance, radius, hardness)` is linear falloff beyond hard radius.
- `localDabBounds(transform, inverse, documentX, documentY, radius, width, height)` projects document-space circle into local-space axis-aligned ellipse via inverse linear rows; `layerBoundsFromDocumentBounds(documentBounds, inverse, layerWidth, layerHeight)` maps document bounds through inverse and expands by 1px for soft-edge aliasing.
- `selectionCoverage(selection, documentX, documentY, regionBuffer?, region?)` returns 1 if no selection, else samples selection coverage store (sparse single-pixel read when no region buffer, or region-buffer lookup); clamps out-of-bounds to 0.
- `readSelectionRegion(selection, dabs, radius)` unions `documentDabBounds` across dabs and reads one selection region; `documentDabBounds(documentX, documentY, radius, canvasWidth, canvasHeight)` clamps to canvas.
- `makePatchFromRegion` / `makeCoveragePatchFromRegion` slice a read region into a patch bounded by `changedBounds`.
- `multiplyTransforms`, `transformPoint`, `invertTransform`, `validateLayer`, `validateTransform` (requires invertible determinant), `validateSelection`, `validateRasterMask`, `validateOutputSize`, `assertFinite`, `assertUnit` all available.
